To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose an essential characteristic, strong relevance, when selecting attribution feature maps, and we propose a new concept, the feature map importance, to refine the contribution, which is faithful and can address the gradient saturation issue.

1) we introduce the Strong Relevance property to select attribution features, and propose a feature map importance ( FMI ) concept to refine attribution features, 2) we propose an attribution method via F MI ( A F MI ), which couples the target with a reference image to assign F MI to the difference from reference at the granularity of the feature map, and 3) A F MI is faithful to the model and superior in explanation performance compared with other attribution methods.

we propose a novel attribution method, termed A Fmi, to address the redundancy of attribution feature and the gradient saturation problems, which couples the reference image with the target image and assigns the Fmi to the "difference of reference" at the level of feature map.
